assessment_summary: In step 0033, the proof makes an incorrect claim about sets. It states that since there are n original vertices in VH, any set of n distinct vertices of G (which has n+17 vertices) must include all the original vertices of VH. This is mathematically false; a subset of size n chosen from a set of size n+17 does not necessarily include all n elements of a specific subset. It could instead include some of the 17 added vertices, thereby omitting some of the original vertices.
counterexample: Let H have n=5 vertices, so G has 5+17 = 22 vertices (5 original and 17 added). A set of 5 distinct vertices of G could consist entirely of 5 of the added vertices. This set does not include all 5 original vertices, contradicting the claim in line 0033.
